query:
I'm working with data that tracks availability periods for various books. Each availability period has a start date and an end date. It's possible for a single book to have multiple availability entries over time.

My goal is to identify books where these availability periods incorrectly overlap. For instance, if book with ID '1' has one availability listed from January 1st to June 30th, and another availability listed from May 1st to December 31st for the same year, that's an overlap I need to find.

I initially tried an approach focusing on books that appear multiple times in the availability data. However, I realized this isn't quite right because a book could legitimately have several distinct availability periods that don't overlap at all (e.g., one period ends in March, and a completely separate one starts in April). My current attempts seem to flag these valid cases incorrectly.

I'm struggling to figure out how to correctly compare the date ranges *within* each book's set of availability records to detect if any of those time periods actually clash.

How can I construct a query to get a list containing only the books (by their ID) that have genuinely overlapping availability date ranges? Ideally, the output would just list the book ID and include a remark like 'Periods Overlap!' for each book identified with this issue.
issue_sql: WITH duplicates AS (SELECT book_id FROM book_availability GROUP BY book_id HAVING COUNT(book_id) > 1) SELECT T1.* FROM book_availability AS T1 INNER JOIN duplicates AS T2 ON T1.book_id = T2.book_id
sol_sql:
SELECT book_id, 'Periods Overlap!' AS remark
FROM (
    SELECT
        *,
        availability_start - LAG(availability_end) OVER (PARTITION BY book_id ORDER BY availability_start NULLS FIRST) AS df
    FROM book_availability
) AS p
GROUP BY book_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN df <= 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0

I'm trying to analyze author performance on our platform by looking at book sales over time. I have access to author information and all the sales records for their titles, including the date each sale occurred.

My goal is to identify the top 3 authors with the highest total sales quantity (sum of units sold) for each year since sales started. I want a result that shows the year, the author's full name, and the total sales quantity attributed to them in that specific year.

I've tried grouping the sales by author and extracting the year from the order date to get total quantities for a particular year, but I'm struggling to figure out how to rank authors *within* each year based on their total sales quantity and then select only the top 3 for *every* year in a single output. I need the final list to be ordered by year, and within each year, by the total quantity (highest first).

How can I construct a query to get this list of the top 3 authors by sales quantity for each year?

query: I'm trying to analyze customer activity by looking at order history over time. I have access to customer information and all the orders they've placed, including the date each order was made. My goal is to identify the top 3 most active customers (by order count) for each year since tracking started. I want a result that shows the year, the customer's full name, and the total number of orders they placed in that specific year. How can I construct a query to get this list of the top 3 customers for each year, ordered by year and then by order count (highest first)?
issue_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(convert_from(co.order_date, 'UTF8') AS TIMESTAMP)), cu.first_name || ' ' || cu.last_name, COUNT(co.order_id) AS nbrOfOrders FROM cust_order AS co INNER JOIN customer AS cu ON co.customer_id = cu.customer_id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(convert_from(co.order_date, 'UTF8') AS TIMESTAMP)) = 2010 GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.first_name, cu.last_name
sol_sql:
SELECT order_year, customer_name, cnt_orders
FROM (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(convert_from(co.order_date, 'UTF8') AS TIMESTAMP)) AS order_year,
        cu.first_name || ' ' || cu.last_name AS customer_name,
        COUNT(co.order_id) AS cnt_orders,
        RANK() OVER (
            PARTITION BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(convert_from(co.order_date, 'UTF8') AS TIMESTAMP))
            ORDER BY COUNT(co.order_id) DESC NULLS LAST
        ) AS rn
    FROM cust_order AS co
    INNER JOIN customer AS cu ON co.customer_id = cu.customer_id
    GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(convert_from(co.order_date, 'UTF8') AS TIMESTAMP)), cu.customer_id, cu.first_name, cu.last_name
) AS ranked_orders
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY order_year NULLS FIRST, cnt_orders DESC NULLS LAST

    WHERE parentid IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT cte.root, t.entityid, t.parentid, t.emission, t.pctcontribution
    FROM cte
    INNER JOIN tree_table AS t ON (t.parentid = cte.entityid)
),
grid AS (
    SELECT
        x.root,
        x.entityid,
        x.parentid,
        x.entity_emission,
        x.groupid,
        x.cumulative_total,
        x.pctcontribution,
        CASE
            WHEN x.entityid = x.root THEN 0
            WHEN x.entityid <> x.root AND x.entityid <> x.groupid AND x.groupid = x.root THEN
                CAST(x.entity_emission * (100 - x.pctcontribution) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(100, 0)
            WHEN x.entityid <> x.root AND x.entityid = x.groupid THEN

                CASE
                    WHEN entityid = root THEN SUM(entity_emission) OVER (PARTITION BY root)

                        CASE

                            ELSE SUM(entity_emission) OVER (PARTITION BY root ORDER BY entityid NULLS FIRST)
                        END
                END
            AS NUMERIC) AS cumulative_total,
            pctcontribution
        FROM cte
        ORDER BY entityid NULLS FIRST

)

            WHEN g.entityid <> g.root AND g.entityid <> g.groupid THEN g.entity_emission
            WHEN g.entityid <> g.root AND g.entityid = g.groupid THEN g.corrected_contribution
            ELSE 0

FROM (

However, I only want to include the components (hours, minutes, seconds) if their value is not zero. For example, if the time value is '01:10:00', the desired output is '1 hours, 10 minutes'. If it's '00:45:15', I'd want '45 minutes, 15 seconds'.

When I've tried to format this, I end up getting strings that include the zero values, like '01 hours, 10 minutes, 00 seconds' or '00 hours, 45 minutes, 15 seconds'. This isn't quite right for my needs.

How can I construct this formatted string in PostgreSQL so that it only shows the non-zero hour, minute, or second parts, joined by commas where necessary?
issue_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(time_val, 'HH24 Hours, MI Minutes, SS Seconds') FROM temp_time_data;

WITH film_actors AS (

        f.film_id, -- atom_id
        fc.category_id, -- molecule_id (from join table)
        f.title, -- element
        STRING_AGG(CAST(fa.actor_id AS TEXT), ',' ORDER BY fa.actor_id NULLS FIRST) AS starring_actor_ids -- connected_bonds (actor IDs)
    FROM film AS f
    LEFT JOIN film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id -- Need category_id early for grouping/joining later
    LEFT JOIN film_actor AS fa ON f.film_id = fa.film_id -- film to actor link
    GROUP BY f.film_id, fc.category_id, f.title -- Group by film, its category, and title
),
category_details AS ( -- Simplified CTE compared to original molecule_stats
    SELECT
        c.category_id, -- molecule_id
        c.name -- label
    FROM category AS c
)
SELECT
    fa_agg.film_id, -- atom_id
    fa_agg.category_id, -- molecule_id
    fa_agg.title, -- element
    cd.name, -- label
    (regexp_split_to_array(fa_agg.starring_actor_ids || ',', ','))[1] AS actor_id, -- bond_id (extract first actor ID)
    a.first_name -- bond_type
FROM film_actors AS fa_agg
JOIN category_details AS cd ON fa_agg.category_id = cd.category_id -- Join aggregated film/actor info with category details
LEFT JOIN actor AS a ON SPLIT_PART(fa_agg.starring_actor_ids || ',', ',', 1) = CAST(a.actor_id AS TEXT) -- Join back to actor using the extracted first actor ID
WHERE fa_agg.film_id IS NOT NULL -- Original had WHERE NOT ab."atom_id" IS NULL, seems redundant after joins but keeping analogous logic

            FROM zip_data AS zd
            WHERE zd.state = 'NY' AND zd.region = 'Northeast' -- Analogous to starting condition

            -- Recursive step: Mimic original join structure
            SELECT
                zd_next.zip_code,
                zd_next.city,
                zd_next.state AS state_abbreviation,
                zd_next.region,
                rh.level + 1,
                rh.path || '->' || CAST(zd_next.zip_code AS VARCHAR(4000))
            FROM region_hierarchy AS rh
            JOIN zip_congress AS zc ON rh.zip_code = zc.zip_code -- Mimics connected

I'm struggling to structure the query to accurately show each title under its publisher, paired correctly with each of its associated sales records.

How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL to effectively join the publisher, title, and sales information to produce a clear list where each row represents a title under a publisher, along with the details of a specific sale associated with that title?
issue_sql:
WITH publisher_titles AS (
    SELECT p.pub_id, p.pub_name, t.title_id, t.title,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.pub_id ORDER BY t.title_id NULLS FIRST) AS title_seq
    FROM publishers AS p
    LEFT JOIN titles AS t ON p.pub_id = t.pub_id
),
title_sales_refined AS (
    SELECT t.pub_id, s.title_id, s.ord_num, s.payterms,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.pub_id ORDER BY s.ord_num NULLS FIRST) AS sale_rank
    FROM titles AS t
    LEFT JOIN sales AS s ON t.title_id = s.title_id
    WHERE t.pub_id IS NOT NULL
),
title_sale_connections AS (
    SELECT pt.pub_id, pt.pub_name, pt.title_id, pt.title,
           tsr.ord_num, tsr.payterms,
           CASE WHEN pt.title_id = tsr.title_id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_connected
    FROM publisher_titles AS pt
    CROSS JOIN title_sales_refined AS tsr
    WHERE pt.pub_id = tsr.pub_id
)

FROM title_sale_connections AS tsc
WHERE tsc.is_connected = 1
UNION ALL
SELECT DISTINCT pt.pub_id, pt.pub_name, pt.title_id, pt.title, NULL AS ord_num, NULL AS payterms
FROM publisher_titles AS pt
WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sales AS s WHERE s.title_id = pt.title_id)
ORDER BY pub_id NULLS FIRST, title_id NULLS FIRST, ord_num NULLS FIRST

I'm working with a dataset of book titles, each having a publication date and a type. My goal is to see how the frequency of each title type has changed over time. Specifically, for every distinct title type, I want to calculate the difference between the number of times that title type was published in its most recent year of publication and the number of times it was published in its earliest year of publication.

However, this doesn't seem right because some title types might not have been published in the absolute earliest or latest year recorded across all titles. The results I'm getting don't seem to reflect the change *within* each type's own publication timeline.

    T1.type AS title_type,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM convert_from(T1.pubdate, 'UTF8')::timestamp) = year_range.recent_year THEN 1 END) -
    COUNT(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM convert_from(T1.pubdate, 'UTF8')::timestamp) = year_range.oldest_year THEN 1 END) AS publication_year_difference
FROM titles AS T1,
    (
        SELECT
            MAX(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM convert_from(pubdate, 'UTF8')::timestamp)) AS recent_year,

query: I'm working with a database that stores book information, including authors for each book. My goal is to find out how many unique pairs of authors have co-authored *at least two different books* together. For example, if Author A and Author B co-authored Book 1, and they also co-authored Book 2, that counts as one such pair. I'm having trouble figuring out how to count these pairs uniquely without counting the same pair twice (A/B and B/A) or counting pairs who only co-authored one book. How can I structure a query to get the total count of unique author pairs who have co-authored two or more distinct books together?
issue_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM book_author ba1
JOIN book_author ba2 ON ba1.book_id = ba2.book_id AND ba1.author_id < ba2.author_id -- Find pairs for the current book
-- Check if this specific pair (ba1.author_id, ba2.author_id) exists for *another* book
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM book_author oba1
    JOIN book_author oba2 ON oba1.book_id = oba2.book_id
    WHERE oba1.author_id = ba1.author_id
      AND oba2.author_id = ba2.author_id
      AND oba1.book_id != ba1.book_id -- Must be a *different* book
);
sol_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        LEAST(ba1.author_id, ba2.author_id) AS author1,
        GREATEST(ba1.author_id, ba2.author_id) AS author2
    FROM book_author ba1
    JOIN book_author ba2 ON ba1.book_id = ba2.book_id AND ba1.author_id != ba2.author_id -- Find pairs on the same book
    -- Check if this pair exists on *another* book
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM book_author oba1
        JOIN book_author oba2 ON oba1.book_id = oba2.book_id
        WHERE LEAST(oba1.author_id, oba2.author_id) = LEAST(ba1.author_id, ba2.author_id)
          AND GREATEST(oba1.author_id, oba2.author_id) = GREATEST(ba1.author_id, ba2.author_id)
          AND oba1.book_id != ba1.book_id -- Must be a *different* book
    )
) AS author_pairs;

query:
I'm working with a dataset of US zip code information in PostgreSQL and I'm trying to identify sequences of consecutive zip codes (ordered numerically) within each state where the population increased between 2010 and 2020. My goal is to get a list showing each state, the starting zip code of such a sequence, the ending zip code of that sequence, and how many zip codes are in that consecutive sequence.

I have records for each zip code, including the state, population in 2010, and population in 2020. I can identify individual zip codes with population increases easily enough (when the 2020 population is greater than the 2010 population).

However, I'm finding it difficult to group these zip codes into *consecutive* sequences based on their numerical order within a state. I've tried ordering the zip codes numerically for each state, but I'm stuck on how to correctly identify where one sequence of increasing population ends and the next one begins, especially after a zip code with a population decrease or no change breaks the sequence. I need to calculate the start zip code, end zip code, and the count of zip codes for only the unbroken sequences of population increase.

How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL to correctly group these consecutive zip codes (ordered numerically) with population increases for each state and calculate the start zip code, end zip code, and the total number of zip codes for each distinct sequence?
issue_sql:
SELECT "state",
       "start_zip",
       "end_zip",
       "zip_count"
FROM "zip_data" MATCH_RECOGNIZE (PARTITION BY "state"
                              ORDER BY "zip_code" MEASURES FIRST("zip_code") AS "start_zip", LAST("zip_code") AS "end_zip", COUNT(*) AS "zip_count" PATTERN (consecutive_increase+) DEFINE consecutive_increase AS "type" = 'STANDARD')
sol_sql:
WITH pop_increase AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    zip_code,
    CASE WHEN population_2020 > population_2010 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_increase,
    CASE WHEN population_2020 > population_2010 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_not_increase
  FROM zip_data
  WHERE population_2020 IS NOT NULL AND population_2010 IS NOT NULL
),
increase_groups AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    zip_code,
    is_increase,
    SUM(is_not_increase) OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY zip_code) AS increase_group
  FROM pop_increase
  WHERE is_increase = 1
),
increase_streaks AS (
  SELECT
    state,
    increase_group,
    MIN(zip_code) AS start_zip,
    MAX(zip_code) AS end_zip,
    COUNT(*) AS zip_count
  FROM increase_groups
  GROUP BY state, increase_group
)
SELECT
  state,
  start_zip,
  end_zip,
  zip_count
FROM increase_streaks
ORDER BY state, start_zip;

query: For each distinct state, I only want to retrieve the first two associated county/zip code records from the `country` table, based on the zip code order. How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL to select only the first two county/zip code records for each state, ordered by their respective zip codes?
issue_sql:
WITH county_stats AS (
    SELECT
        state,
        COUNT(*) AS county_count,
        (array_agg(county ORDER BY zip_code))[1] AS first_county,
        (array_agg(county ORDER BY zip_code DESC))[1] AS last_county
    FROM "country"
    GROUP BY state
),
ranked_counties AS (
    SELECT
        c."zip_code",
        c."state",
        c."county",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c."state" ORDER BY c."zip_code") AS county_rank,
        stats.county_count,
        stats.first_county,
        stats.last_county
    FROM "country" c
    JOIN county_stats stats ON c."state" = stats.state
),
filtered_counties AS (
    SELECT
        rc.*,
        CASE
            WHEN rc.county_rank <= 2 THEN 'TOP'
            WHEN rc.county_rank > rc.county_count - 2 THEN 'BOTTOM'
            ELSE 'MIDDLE'
        END AS position,
        LAG(rc."county") OVER (PARTITION BY rc."state" ORDER BY rc."zip_code") AS prev_county,
        LEAD(rc."county") OVER (PARTITION BY rc."state" ORDER BY rc."zip_code") AS next_county
    FROM ranked_counties rc
)
SELECT
    fc."zip_code",
    fc."state",
    fc."county",
    fc.county_rank AS rnk,
    fc.position,
    fc.prev_county,
    fc.next_county,
    fc.first_county,
    fc.last_county
FROM filtered_counties fc
WHERE fc.county_rank <= 2
GROUP BY
    fc."zip_code",
    fc."state",
    fc."county",
    fc.county_rank,
    fc.position,
    fc.prev_county,
    fc.next_county,
    fc.first_county,
    fc.last_county
ORDER BY fc."state", fc.county_rank
sol_sql:
SELECT *
FROM
    (SELECT
        c.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY c.state
            ORDER BY c.zip_code
        ) AS rnk
    FROM country c) subquery
WHERE rnk <= 2

WITH sale_dates AS (
    SELECT t.pub_id,
           s.ord_date,
           s.title_id,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.pub_id ORDER BY CAST(s.ord_date AS TEXT) DESC) AS sale_rank
    FROM sales s
    JOIN titles t ON s.title_id = t.title_id
    WHERE s.ord_date IS NOT NULL AND t.pub_id IS NOT NULL
),
publisher_stats AS (
    SELECT p.pub_id,
           p.pub_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT t.title_id) AS title_count
    FROM publishers p
    LEFT JOIN titles t ON p.pub_id = t.pub_id
    GROUP BY p.pub_id, p.pub_name
),
sale_summary AS (
    SELECT sd.pub_id,
           sd.ord_date,
           sd.sale_rank,
           string_agg(t.title, ', ' ORDER BY t.title) AS titles_sold
    FROM sale_dates sd
    JOIN titles t ON sd.title_id = t.title_id
    WHERE sd.sale_rank <= 2
    GROUP BY sd.pub_id, sd.ord_date, sd.sale_rank
)
SELECT ps.pub_id,
       ps.pub_name,
       MAX(CASE WHEN ss.sale_rank = 1 THEN CAST(ss.ord_date AS TEXT) END) AS last_sale_date,
       MAX(CASE WHEN ss.sale_rank = 1 THEN ss.titles_sold END) AS last_sale_titles,
       MAX(CASE WHEN ss.sale_rank = 2 THEN CAST(ss.ord_date AS TEXT) END) AS prev_sale_date,
       MAX(CASE WHEN ss.sale_rank = 2 THEN ss.titles_sold END) AS prev_sale_titles,
       ps.title_count
FROM publisher_stats ps
LEFT JOIN sale_summary ss ON ps.pub_id = ss.pub_id
GROUP BY ps.pub_id, ps.pub_name, ps.title_count

ORDER BY MAX(CASE WHEN ss.sale_rank = 1 THEN CAST(ss.ord_date AS TEXT) END) DESC

SELECT

    MAX(CASE
        WHEN rn = 1 THEN CAST(ord_date AS TEXT)
    END) AS last_sale_date,
    MAX(CASE
        WHEN rn = 2 THEN CAST(ord_date AS TEXT)
    END) AS prev_sale_date
FROM
    (SELECT
        t.pub_id,
        s.ord_date,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY t.pub_id
            ORDER BY CAST(s.ord_date AS TEXT) DESC
        ) AS rn
    FROM sales s
    JOIN titles t ON s.title_id = t.title_id
    WHERE t.pub_id IS NOT NULL AND s.ord_date IS NOT NULL) subquery
WHERE rn <= 2
GROUP BY pub_id

WITH game_years AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT -- Need distinct years per region
        pr.region_id,
        g.games_year,
        e.sport_id,
        g.season,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY pr.region_id ORDER BY g.games_year DESC) AS game_rank
    FROM person_region AS pr
    JOIN person AS p ON pr.person_id = p.id
    JOIN games_competitor AS gc ON p.id = gc.person_id
    JOIN games AS g ON gc.games_id = g.id
    JOIN competitor_event AS ce ON gc.id = ce.competitor_id
    JOIN event AS e ON ce.event_id = e.id
    WHERE g.games_year IS NOT NULL
),
region_stats AS (
    SELECT
        nr.id AS region_id,
        nr.region_name,
        COUNT(DISTINCT e.sport_id) AS sport_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT g.season) AS season_count
    FROM noc_region AS nr
    LEFT JOIN person_region AS pr ON nr.id = pr.region_id
    LEFT JOIN person AS p ON pr.person_id = p.id
    LEFT JOIN games_competitor AS gc ON p.id = gc.person_id
    LEFT JOIN games AS g ON gc.games_id = g.id
    LEFT JOIN competitor_event AS ce ON gc.id = ce.competitor_id
    LEFT JOIN event AS e ON ce.event_id = e.id
    GROUP BY nr.id, nr.region_name
),
game_summary AS (
    SELECT
        gy.region_id,
        gy.games_year,
        gy.game_rank,
        string_agg(sp.sport_name, ', ' ORDER BY sp.sport_name) AS sports_participated
    FROM game_years gy
    JOIN sport sp ON gy.sport_id = sp.id
    WHERE gy.game_rank <= 2
    GROUP BY gy.region_id, gy.games_year, gy.game_rank
)
SELECT
    rs.region_id,
    rs.region_name,
    MAX(CASE WHEN gs.game_rank = 1 THEN gs.games_year END) AS last_game_year,
    MAX(CASE WHEN gs.game_rank = 1 THEN gs.sports_participated END) AS last_game_sports,
    MAX(CASE WHEN gs.game_rank = 2 THEN gs.games_year END) AS prev_game_year,
    MAX(CASE WHEN gs.game_rank = 2 THEN gs.sports_participated END) AS prev_game_sports,
    rs.sport_count,
    rs.season_count
FROM region_stats rs
LEFT JOIN game_summary gs ON rs.region_id = gs.region_id
GROUP BY rs.region_id, rs.region_name, rs.sport_count, rs.season_count
HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN gs.game_rank = 1 THEN gs.games_year END) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY MAX(CASE WHEN gs.game_rank = 1 THEN gs.games_year END) DESC

SELECT
    region_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN games_year END) AS last_game_year,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN games_year END) AS prev_game_year
FROM (
    SELECT
        region_id,
        games_year,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region_id ORDER BY games_year DESC) AS rn
    FROM (
        SELECT DISTINCT
            pr.region_id,
            g.games_year
        FROM person_region AS pr
        JOIN person AS p ON pr.person_id = p.id
        JOIN games_competitor AS gc ON p.id = gc.person_id
        JOIN games AS g ON gc.games_id = g.id
        WHERE g.games_year IS NOT NULL
    ) AS distinct_region_years
) AS ranked_years
WHERE rn <= 2
GROUP BY region_id

query:
I'm trying to process a set of date ranges, each defined by a start date and an end date. My objective is to determine the continuous time periods resulting from these ranges and calculate a cumulative count that reflects how many ranges are active within each period. Essentially, the count should increase when a range starts and decrease when it ends.

Ultimately, I need a result that lists only those periods where this cumulative count is greater than zero. Each row in the result should show the start date of the period, the end date of the period, and the corresponding positive cumulative count. I also need to handle the validity of these resulting periods correctly – the start date should be less than or equal to the end date, although sometimes a period might not have an end date (represented as null).

I've attempted to use window functions to keep track of this running count based on the original start and end dates, and also to figure out the correct end date for each distinct period where the count remains constant. However, I'm finding it tricky to get the logic right and I'm not getting the intervals and counts I expect. It feels like I'm missing a step in how to properly calculate these continuous periods and their associated counts.

Could someone explain how I can structure a PostgreSQL query to take these initial start/end date pairs, calculate the cumulative count over the timeline they define, and then output just the valid periods (start date, end date, count) where the count is positive?
issue_sql:
SELECT "valid_from",
       "valid_until",
       "count"
FROM
  (SELECT "dt" AS "valid_from",
          LEAD("dt") OVER (
                           ORDER BY "dt") - INTERVAL '1' SECOND AS "valid_until",
          SUM("count" * "type") OVER (
                                      ORDER BY "dt") AS "count"
   FROM
     (SELECT "valid_from",
             "valid_until" + INTERVAL '1 DAY' AS "valid_until",
             1 AS "count"
      FROM
        (SELECT TO_DATE('2014-01-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "valid_from",
                TO_DATE('2014-01-31', 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "valid_until"
         FROM zip_data
         UNION ALL SELECT TO_DATE('2014-02-01', 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "valid_from",
                          TO_DATE('2014-02-28', 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "valid_until"
         FROM zip_data)))
WHERE "count" > 0
  AND ("valid_from" <= "valid_until"
       OR "valid_until" IS NULL)
sol_sql:
WITH date_ranges AS (
    SELECT
        DATE '2014-01-01' AS valid_from,
        DATE '2014-01-31' AS valid_until
    UNION ALL
    SELECT
        DATE '2014-02-01' AS valid_from,
        DATE '2014-02-28' AS valid_until
),
unpivoted AS (
    SELECT valid_from AS dt, 1 AS type
    FROM date_ranges
    UNION ALL
    SELECT valid_until + INTERVAL '1 day' AS dt, -1 AS type
    FROM date_ranges
),
running_totals AS (
    SELECT
        dt AS valid_from,
        LEAD(dt) OVER (ORDER BY dt) - INTERVAL '1 second' AS valid_until,
        SUM(type) OVER (ORDER BY dt) AS count
    FROM unpivoted
)
SELECT
    valid_from,
    valid_until,
    count
FROM running_totals
WHERE count > 0
AND (valid_from <= valid_until OR valid_until IS NULL);

query:
I'm working with PostgreSQL and trying to figure out if a few specific columns – namely 'zip_code', 'city', and 'state' – exist within the 'zip_data' table in my database. My goal is to get a result that clearly shows whether each of these columns is present, ideally in a single row format where each column name corresponds to one of the columns I'm checking, and the value indicates if it exists (like 'YES' or 'NO').

I've looked into querying system information tables to get column details, which seems promising for finding out if a column exists individually. However, I'm running into trouble when trying to consolidate this information into the specific single-row output I need. Instead of getting one summary row, my attempts often result in multiple rows, one for each column I check, or I just can't figure out how to transform the existence check results into separate columns in one row.

How can I structure a query to check for the presence of 'zip_code', 'city', and 'state' in the 'zip_data' table and display the outcome as a single row with columns like `zip_code`, `city`, and `state`, showing 'YES' or 'NO' for each based on whether they exist?
issue_sql:
WITH "columns" ("column_name") AS
  (SELECT 'zip_code'
   UNION ALL SELECT 'city'
   UNION ALL SELECT 'state'),
     "column_exists" ("column_name",
                      "column_exists") AS
  (SELECT c."column_name",
          COALESCE(a.attname, 'NO')
   FROM "columns" c
   LEFT OUTER JOIN pg_attribute a ON (a.attrelid = 'zip_data'::regclass
                                      AND c."column_name" = a.attname))
SELECT *
FROM "column_exists"
PIVOT (MAX("column_exists")
       FOR "column_name" IN ('zip_code', 'city', 'state'))
WHERE
    (SELECT "column_name"
     FROM "columns") = 'zip_code';
sol_sql:
WITH columns AS (
    SELECT 'zip_code' AS column_name
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'city'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'state'
),

column_exists AS (
    SELECT
        c.column_name,
        CASE WHEN a.column_name IS NOT NULL THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END AS column_exists
    FROM columns c
    LEFT OUTER JOIN information_schema.columns a
        ON (
            a.table_name = 'zip_data'
            AND c.column_name = a.column_name
            AND a.table_schema = current_schema()
        )
)

SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN column_name = 'zip_code' THEN column_exists END) AS zip_code,
    MAX(CASE WHEN column_name = 'city' THEN column_exists END) AS city,
    MAX(CASE WHEN column_name = 'state' THEN column_exists END) AS state
FROM column_exists;

My goal is to get a result containing only the numbers that appear in both strings. For the example strings, the expected output would be the values '36' and '98'.

How can I effectively compare these two strings in PostgreSQL to extract only the values they have in common?
issue_sql:
WITH string1_tab AS (
    SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR('24,36,78,98', '[^,]+', 1, generate_series) AS value,
           generate_series AS position
    FROM generate_series(1, LENGTH('24,36,78,98') - LENGTH(REPLACE('24,36,78,98', ',', '')) + 1)
),
string2_tab AS (
    SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR('25,36,88,98', '[^,]+', 1, generate_series) AS value,
           generate_series AS position
    FROM generate_series(1, LENGTH('25,36,88,98') - LENGTH(REPLACE('25,36,88,98', ',', '')) + 1)
),
string1_parsed AS (
    SELECT TO_NUMBER(TRIM(value), '999999') AS num_value
    FROM string1_tab
),
string2_parsed AS (
    SELECT TO_NUMBER(TRIM(value), '999999') AS num_value
    FROM string2_tab
),
common_values AS (
    SELECT s1.num_value
    FROM string1_parsed s1
    JOIN string2_parsed s2 ON s1.num_value = s2.num_value
)

FROM common_values
WHERE num_value IS NOT NULL

Furthermore, I need to calculate a flag ('Y' or 'N') for each sale based on some conditions derived using window functions. Specifically, I need to look at groups of sales based on their order date (ignoring the time part) and the order number. Within each group, I need to find the minimum duration (days from order date to current date) and also count how many records share the exact same date, order number, and calculated duration.

The flag should be 'Y' if either the minimum duration calculated for that date/order number group is zero, OR if the count calculated for that specific record's date/order number/duration combination is greater than one. Otherwise, the flag should be 'N'.

I've been trying to structure this using window functions after converting the bytea date, but I'm running into difficulties getting the calculations for the minimum duration and the counts within the partitions correct, especially with the date conversion involved. I'm not getting the results I expect for the flag.

          ord_num AS code,
          CURRENT_DATE - CAST(convert_from(ord_date, 'UTF8') AS DATE) AS duration,

If a zip code is associated with fewer than three area codes, the remaining area code columns for that zip code should be empty or null. If a zip code is associated with more than three area codes, I only want to see the first three in the output, based on their order. Finally, the entire result set should be ordered by the zip code.

I've tried arranging the data, perhaps using some conditional logic to assign area codes to different columns, but I'm struggling to get it right. My attempts haven't correctly limited the results to the first three area codes per zip code, nor have they properly handled cases with fewer than three area codes by filling with nulls. The grouping per zip code isn't working as expected.

issue_sql:
SELECT "zip_code",
    "area_code_1",
    "area_code_2",
    "area_code_3"
FROM (
    SELECT "zip_code", "area_code",
           CASE WHEN "area_code" = 1 THEN "area_code" END AS "area_code_1",
           CASE WHEN "area_code" = 2 THEN "area_code" END AS "area_code_2",

FROM (
    SELECT "zip_code", "area_code",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "zip_code" ORDER BY "area_code") AS rn
    FROM "area_code"
) AS subquery

WITH RECURSIVE PublisherTotals AS (
  SELECT
    P.publisher_name,
    SUM(OL.price) AS total_price
  FROM publisher AS P
  JOIN book AS B ON P.publisher_id = B.publisher_id
  JOIN order_line AS OL ON B.book_id = OL.book_id
  WHERE P.publisher_name IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY P.publisher_name
),
OrderedPublishers AS (
  SELECT
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY publisher_name DESC) AS rn,
    publisher_name,
    total_price
  FROM PublisherTotals
),
RecursiveCTE AS (
  SELECT
    rn,
    publisher_name,
    total_price,
    total_price AS cumulative_total,
    CASE
      WHEN total_price <= 800 THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS included
  FROM OrderedPublishers
  WHERE rn = 1

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    op.rn,
    op.publisher_name,
    op.total_price,
    CASE
      WHEN r.cumulative_total + op.total_price <= 800 THEN r.cumulative_total + op.total_price
      ELSE r.cumulative_total
    END AS cumulative_total,
    CASE
      WHEN r.cumulative_total + op.total_price <= 800 THEN 1 ELSE 0
    END AS included
  FROM RecursiveCTE r
  JOIN OrderedPublishers op ON op.rn = r.rn + 1
)
SELECT publisher_name, total_price
FROM RecursiveCTE
WHERE included = 1
ORDER BY rn;

WITH "my_table" AS (
    SELECT 'A' AS "cto", 1 AS "nif", 'A1' AS "file_", 5 AS "filesize"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'A' AS "cto", 1 AS "nif", 'A2' AS "file_", 3 AS "filesize"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'A' AS "cto", 2 AS "nif", 'A3' AS "file_", 2 AS "filesize"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'A' AS "cto", 2 AS "nif", 'A4' AS "file_", 1 AS "filesize"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'B' AS "cto", 1 AS "nif", 'B1' AS "file_", 4 AS "filesize"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'B' AS "cto", 1 AS "nif", 'B2' AS "file_", 6 AS "filesize"
),
ranked_data AS (
    SELECT
        t.*,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "cto" ORDER BY SUBSTRING("file_", 1, 1), CAST(SUBSTRING("file_", 2) AS INTEGER)) AS "rn",
        SUM("filesize") OVER (PARTITION BY "nif") AS "nif_size"
    FROM "my_table" t
),
with_lag AS (
    SELECT
        rd.*,
        LAG(rd."nif", 1, rd."nif") OVER (PARTITION BY rd."cto" ORDER BY rd."rn") AS "prev_nif"
    FROM ranked_data rd
),
partition_groups AS (
    SELECT
        wl.*,

For example, if I have an input string like 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|Address at some where|details', the result I'm looking for is 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|Address at some where'. Another example might be 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|', where the expected output would be the same string 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|'. If the string has fewer than five parts, like 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16', I'd want the entire string back.

I've tried using regular expressions to isolate this part of the string, but I'm having trouble getting it right consistently. Sometimes my attempts seem to match incorrectly or don't properly anchor the match to the start of the string, leading to unexpected results depending on the exact content and length of the input string.

How can I reliably extract exactly the first five pipe-separated values (or fewer, if the string has less than five) from the beginning of these strings?

For example, if I have an input string like 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|Address at some where|details', the result I'm looking for is 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|Address at some where'. Another example might be 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|', where the expected output would be the same string 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|'. If the string has fewer than five parts, like 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16', I'd want the entire string back.

I've tried using regular expressions to isolate this part of the string, but I'm having trouble getting it right consistently. Sometimes my attempts seem to match incorrectly or don't properly anchor the match to the start of the string, leading to unexpected results depending on the exact content and length of the input string.

How can I reliably extract exactly the first five pipe-separated values (or fewer, if the string has less than five) from the beginning of these strings?
issue_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE "a" ("test") AS
  (SELECT 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|Address at some where|details '
   UNION ALL SELECT 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|'
   UNION ALL SELECT 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16'
   UNION ALL SELECT "test" || '|MoreData'
   FROM "a")
SELECT "test",
       REGEXP_SUBSTR("test", '([^|]+\|?){1,5}') AS "res"
FROM "a"
sol_sql:
WITH a (
    "test") AS (
    SELECT 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|Address at some where|details'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16|DY7009|'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'Jack|Sparrow|17-09-16'
)

SELECT
    "test",
    SUBSTRING("test" FROM '^(([^|]+\|?){1,5})') AS "res"
FROM a
test_cases:
def test_case(pred_sqls, sol_sqls, db_name, conn):
    pred_sqls = remove_distinct(pred_sqls)
    sol_sqls = remove_distinct(sol_sqls)
    result = ex_base(pred_sqls, sol_sqls, db_name, conn)
    assert result == 1, f"ex_base returned {result} but expected 1."
    return result

query:
I'm working with two tables that track user logins and group associations. One table (`login`) holds login details, including a unique identifier (`guid`), a login name (`login`), and a person's name (`name`). It seems I have some duplicate entries in this table where the `login` name and person's `name` are identical, but they have different unique identifiers (`guid`).

Another table (`groups`) links these unique identifiers (`guid` from the `login` table, referred to as `room_guid` in the `groups` table) to a different user identifier (`user_guid`). The issue I'm facing is that for the duplicate `login`/`name` pairs, only one of the associated `guid`s seems to be present in the `groups` table (as `room_guid`).

My goal is to add the missing `guid`s (the ones belonging to the duplicate `login`/`name` pairs but not currently in the `groups` table) into the `groups` table. Critically, when I add a missing `guid`, I need to associate it with the *same* `user_guid` that its duplicate counterpart (the one already present in the `groups` table) is linked to.

I've managed to identify which `guid`s are part of these duplicate sets and are currently missing from the `groups` table. However, I'm stuck on how to correctly retrieve the corresponding `user_guid` from the *existing* entry for the duplicate record and use that when inserting the new row for the missing `guid`.

How can I structure an insertion operation to add these missing `guid`s into the `groups` table, ensuring each new entry gets the correct `user_guid` based on its duplicate partner that's already there?
issue_sql: SELECT guid FROM login WHERE (login, name) IN (SELECT login, name FROM login GROUP BY login, name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AND NOT guid IN (SELECT room_guid FROM groups)
sol_sql:
INSERT INTO groups (room_guid, user_guid)
SELECT
    missing_login.guid, -- The guid that needs to be inserted
    existing_group.user_guid -- The user_guid from the existing duplicate
FROM
    login AS missing_login
JOIN
    login AS existing_login ON missing_login.login = existing_login.login AND missing_login.name = existing_login.name AND missing_login.guid != existing_login.guid
JOIN
    groups AS existing_group ON existing_login.guid = existing_group.room_guid
WHERE
    missing_login.guid NOT IN (SELECT room_guid FROM groups);

query:
I'm working with two tables that track user logins and group associations. One table, `login`, holds login details, including a unique identifier (`guid`), a login name (`login`), and a person's name (`name`). It seems I have some duplicate entries in this table where the login name and person's name are identical, but they have different unique identifiers (`guid`).

Another table, `groups`, links these unique identifiers (`guid` from the `login` table, referred to as `room_guid` here) to a different user identifier (`user_guid`). The issue I'm facing is that for the duplicate login/name pairs, only one of the associated `guid`s seems to be present in the `groups` table (as `room_guid`).

My goal is to add the missing `guid`s (the ones belonging to the duplicate login/name pairs but not currently in the `groups` table) into the `groups` table. Critically, when I add a missing `guid`, I need to associate it with the *same* `user_guid` that its duplicate counterpart (the one already present in the `groups` table) is linked to.

I've managed to identify which `guid`s are part of these duplicate sets and are currently missing from the `groups` table. However, I'm stuck on how to correctly retrieve the corresponding `user_guid` from the *existing* entry for the duplicate record and use that when inserting the new row for the missing `guid`.

How can I structure an insertion operation to add these missing `guid`s into the groups table, ensuring each new entry gets the correct `user_guid` based on its duplicate partner that's already there?
issue_sql: SELECT guid FROM login WHERE (login, name) IN (SELECT login, name FROM login GROUP BY login, name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AND NOT guid IN (SELECT room_guid FROM groups)
sol_sql: INSERT INTO groups (room_guid, user_guid) SELECT o.guid, g.user_guid FROM login AS o JOIN groups AS g ON o.login = (SELECT o2.login FROM login AS o2 WHERE o2.guid = g.room_guid) AND o.name = (SELECT o3.name FROM login AS o3 WHERE o3.guid = g.room_guid) WHERE NOT o.guid IN (SELECT room_guid FROM groups)

I'm working with two temporary tables that track user details and elite status years. One table, `Users_temp`, holds user details, including a unique identifier (`user_id`), their average review stars (`user_average_stars`), and their review count category (`user_review_count`). It seems I have some duplicate entries in this table where the average stars and review count category are identical, but they have different unique identifiers (`user_id`).

Another table, `Elite_temp`, links these unique identifiers (`user_id` from the first table) to a specific year (`year_id`) when the user achieved elite status. The issue I'm facing is that for the duplicate average stars/review count pairs, only one of the associated `user_id`s seems to be present in the `Elite_temp` table.

My goal is to add the missing `user_id`s (the ones belonging to the duplicate average stars/review count pairs but not currently in the `Elite_temp` table) into the `Elite_temp` table. Critically, when I add a missing `user_id`, I need to associate it with the *same* `year_id` that its duplicate counterpart (the one already present in the `Elite_temp` table) is linked to.

I've managed to identify which `user_id`s are part of these duplicate sets and are currently missing from the `Elite_temp` table. However, I'm stuck on how to correctly retrieve the corresponding `year_id` from the *existing* entry for the duplicate record and use that when inserting the new row for the missing `user_id`.

How can I structure an insertion operation to add these missing `user_id`s into the `Elite_temp` table, ensuring each new entry gets the correct `year_id` based on its duplicate partner that's already there?

query: I'm trying to analyze zip code records based on their zip code and employee count. My goal is to find all records that belong to a sequence of *three or more consecutive* zip codes, where *each* record in that sequence has an `employees` count greater than 100. I know how to filter records where the employee count is over 100, but I'm having trouble identifying only those records that are part of a consecutive run of at least three based on their zip code. For instance, if zip codes 5, 6, 7, and 8 all meet the >100 condition, I'd want all four returned because they form a consecutive sequence of 3 or more. However, a zip code record like 10, which might have >100 employees but isn't part of a consecutive block of at least three such records (e.g., zip codes 9 or 11 don't meet the condition), should be excluded. How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL to select only those zip code records that satisfy the >100 employee condition *and* are part of a group of at least three records with consecutive zip codes?
issue_sql: SELECT zip_code, city, employees, CASE WHEN employees > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS emp_flag, SUM(CASE WHEN employees > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (ORDER BY zip_code NULLS FIRST) AS grp, zip_code - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY zip_code NULLS FIRST) AS diff, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN employees > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ORDER BY city NULLS FIRST) AS sal_rn, zip_code - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CASE WHEN employees > 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ORDER BY city NULLS FIRST) AS sal_grp FROM zip_data
sol_sql: WITH temp AS (SELECT b.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY zip_code NULLS FIRST) - zip_code AS grp FROM zip_data AS b WHERE employees > 100), temp2 AS (SELECT a.*, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY grp) AS cnt FROM temp AS a) SELECT zip_code, city, employees FROM temp2 WHERE cnt >= 3 ORDER BY zip_code NULLS FIRST

query: I'm trying to analyze abbreviation records based on their Code and Type. My goal is to find all records that belong to a sequence of *three or more consecutive* Codes (based on the numeric part of the Code), *within the same Type*, where *each* record in that sequence has a `Fullname` length greater than 5. How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL to select only those abbreviation records that satisfy the `LENGTH(Fullname) > 5` condition *and* are part of a group of at least three records with consecutive Codes within their Type?
issue_sql: SELECT Type, Code, Fullname, CASE WHEN LENGTH(Fullname) > 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS name_flag, SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(Fullname) > 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY Type ORDER BY CAST(substring(Code from 2) AS INTEGER) NULLS FIRST) AS grp, CAST(substring(Code from 2) AS INTEGER) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Type ORDER BY CAST(substring(Code from 2) AS INTEGER) NULLS FIRST) AS diff, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Type, CASE WHEN LENGTH(Fullname) > 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ORDER BY CAST(substring(Code from 2) AS INTEGER) NULLS FIRST) AS name_rn, CAST(substring(Code from 2) AS INTEGER) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Type, CASE WHEN LENGTH(Fullname) > 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ORDER BY CAST(substring(Code from 2) AS INTEGER) NULLS FIRST) AS name_grp FROM abbrev

query:
I'm working with some movie data where I have records describing film metrics. Each film might have an entry for its 'replacement_cost' and 'rental_rate', identified by a text description like 'film1_replacement_cost' and 'film1_rental_rate', along with the corresponding monetary value.

My goal is to calculate a 'cost_rate_ratio' for each film by dividing its replacement cost value by its rental rate value. For instance, if 'film1_replacement_cost' has a value of 20.99 and 'film1_rental_rate' has a value of 0.99, the ratio for 'film1' should be calculated as 20.99 divided by 0.99.

I need the final result set to show all the original metric records, and additionally, include these newly calculated ratio records, perhaps identified with a description like 'film1_cost_rate_ratio' and its corresponding calculated value.

I've attempted to group the records based on the common identifier (like 'film1') to perform the division, but I'm running into issues getting the correct pairs of replacement cost and rental rate values associated for the calculation. Combining these calculated ratios back with the original data in the desired format is also proving difficult.

How can I structure a query to correctly calculate this ratio for each film (replacement cost value / rental rate value) and display these ratios alongside all the original metric entries?
issue_sql:
select "metric_key", "metric_value"
    from "film_metrics"
    union all

    select
        substring("metric_key", 1, position('_' in "metric_key") - 1) ||'_cost_rate_ratio' as metric_key,
        max(case when substring("metric_key", -4) = 'cost' then "metric_value" end) /
        max(case when substring("metric_key", -4) = 'rate' then "metric_value" end) as "metric_value"
    from "film_metrics"
    group by substring("metric_key", 1, position('_' in "metric_key") - 1)
sol_sql:
SELECT "metric_key", "metric_value"
FROM "film_metrics"

UNION ALL

SELECT
    split_part("metric_key", '_', 1) || '_cost_rate_ratio' AS metric_key,
    MAX(CASE WHEN "metric_key" LIKE '%_replacement_cost' THEN "metric_value" END) /
    MAX(CASE WHEN "metric_key" LIKE '%_rental_rate' THEN "metric_value" END) AS "metric_value"
FROM "film_metrics"
GROUP BY split_part("metric_key", '_', 1)

WITH yearly_data AS (
  SELECT

    COUNT(*) AS count_value

  GROUP BY games_year
)

  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2002 THEN count_value ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "2002",
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2004 THEN count_value ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "2004",

  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2008 THEN count_value ELSE 0 END), 0) AS "2008",
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN year IN (2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008) THEN count_value ELSE 0 END), 0) AS for_total
FROM yearly_data

query:
I'm trying to create a PostgreSQL function that acts like a lookup tool for the `abbrev` table. It needs to accept values for `Type` and `Code` to filter rows. Besides the filter values, the function also takes a parameter telling it *which* column's value I want it to return (e.g., 'TYPE', 'CODE', or 'FULLNAME').

My goal is for the function to find the first row matching the provided `Type` and `Code` criteria and then return the value from the specific column I requested. For example, if I pass in 'POS', 'C', and 'FULLNAME' as the requested column, it should find the matching row and return the value from its `Fullname` column ('Center'). If I pass 'TEAM', 'EDM', and 'TYPE', it should filter using 'TEAM' and 'EDM' and return the value from the `Type` column ('TEAM').

I've been trying to build this logic inside a PL/pgSQL function, figuring out how to return the value from the column specified by the input parameter. However, I'm running into issues getting the correct value back from the function based on the requested column name parameter. It seems more complicated than I initially thought, especially handling the dynamic part of which column to return based on an input string.

How can I structure this PostgreSQL function correctly to filter based on `Type` and `Code` and return the value from the specific column indicated by the function's parameter?
sol_sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION FIND_ABBREV_COLUMN(
    IN_TYPE TEXT,
    IN_CODE TEXT,
    IN_REQUESTED_COLUMN TEXT
) RETURNS TEXT AS $$
DECLARE
    result TEXT;
BEGIN
    SELECT
        CASE UPPER(IN_REQUESTED_COLUMN) -- Use UPPER for case-insensitivity
            WHEN 'TYPE' THEN Type
            WHEN 'CODE' THEN Code
            WHEN 'FULLNAME' THEN Fullname
            ELSE NULL
        END
    INTO result
    FROM abbrev
    WHERE Type = IN_TYPE
      AND Code = IN_CODE
    LIMIT 1;

    RETURN result;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

query:
I'm working with state abbreviations in my PostgreSQL database and need to generate a unique hash for each one, primarily for data integrity purposes.

My requirement is that the resulting hash must be exactly 8 bytes long. I've tried using the standard SHA1 hashing mechanism available, but the hash it generates is much longer than the 8 bytes I need. I'm a bit stuck on how to get a hash of the specific length required.

Is there a straightforward way in PostgreSQL to generate an SHA1 hash for my state abbreviations but ensure the final output is precisely 8 bytes long?
issue_sql: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;
SELECT digest(abbreviation::bytea, 'sha1') AS hash_value, length(digest(abbreviation::bytea, 'sha1')) AS hash_length FROM state;
sol_sql: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;
SELECT substring(digest(abbreviation::bytea, 'sha1') from 1 for 8) AS hash_value, length(substring(digest(abbreviation::bytea, 'sha1') from 1 for 8)) AS hash_length FROM state;

query: I'm working with a dataset of book titles, and some titles are missing entries in the notes field. My goal is to fill these missing notes. Specifically, when a title record has a missing note, I want to populate it with the note from the *next* title record in sequence (ordered by the title identifier). However, the challenge is that the immediately following title might *also* have a missing note. In that case, I need to look at the title after that, and so on, until I find the first subsequent title that actually has a note recorded. I've tried a couple of ways to look ahead to the next record to grab the note, but my attempts haven't quite handled the situation where multiple consecutive titles might be missing notes. It seems like I'm only getting the value from the very next row, regardless of whether it's missing or not, instead of finding the *first available* note from the following records. How can I structure a query to correctly fill in the missing notes for a title using the note from the first subsequent title that has a non-missing note, based on the title identifier order?
issue_sql: SELECT title_id, notes, CASE WHEN notes IS NULL THEN LEAD(notes) OVER (ORDER BY title_id ASC NULLS FIRST) ELSE notes END AS imputed_notes FROM titles ORDER BY title_id NULLS FIRST
sol_sql: SELECT e.title_id, COALESCE(e.notes, (SELECT e2.notes FROM titles AS e2 WHERE e2.title_id > e.title_id AND NOT e2.notes IS NULL ORDER BY e2.title_id ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1)) AS imputed_notes FROM titles AS e ORDER BY e.title_id ASC NULLS FIRST

query: I'm working with Olympic participation data and need help categorizing participations for each athlete. My goal is to label each participation as either 'New' or 'Followup'. The logic should be: the very first participation recorded for any given athlete is always considered 'New'. Subsequent participations for that same athlete should be labeled 'Followup' but only if they occur within 4 years (i.e., the next Olympic cycle) of the *immediately preceding* participation for that athlete. If more than 4 years pass between two consecutive participations for an athlete, the later participation should be marked as 'New', effectively restarting the sequence. I've tried comparing participation years against the earliest participation year for each athlete, but this doesn't capture the rolling 4-year window correctly. It fails to identify 'Followup' participations properly when multiple occur close together, and it doesn't reset to 'New' after a gap longer than 4 years. I'm finding it tricky to set up the comparison between a participation and the one right before it for the same athlete. How can I structure a query in PostgreSQL to correctly apply this 'New'/'Followup' logic based on the 4-year gap from the *previous* participation within each athlete's record?
issue_sql: SELECT T1.id, T1.person_id, T2.games_year, CASE WHEN (T2.games_year - MIN(T2.games_year) OVER (PARTITION BY T1.person_id)) <= 4 THEN 'Followup' ELSE 'New' END AS Category FROM games_competitor AS T1 INNER JOIN games AS T2 ON T1.games_id = T2.id ORDER BY T1.id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 10
sol_sql: WITH RankedParticipations AS (SELECT T1.id, T1.person_id, T2.games_year, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY T1.person_id ORDER BY T2.games_year NULLS FIRST) AS rn, LAG(T2.games_year) OVER (PARTITION BY T1.person_id ORDER BY T2.games_year NULLS FIRST) AS prev_year FROM games_competitor AS T1 INNER JOIN games AS T2 ON T1.games_id = T2.id), CategorizedParticipations AS (SELECT id, person_id, games_year, CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN 'New' WHEN (games_year - prev_year) <= 4 THEN 'Followup' ELSE 'New' END AS Category FROM RankedParticipations) SELECT * FROM CategorizedParticipations ORDER BY id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 10

I'm working with a database containing US address information, including zip codes, area codes, and counties. I need to retrieve a sequence of area codes and their corresponding county details for a specific zip code, identified as '501'.

My goal is to get a list that shows each area code associated with the zip code, alongside the county name and state associated with that position in the sequence. Essentially, I want to see the area codes and county information laid out in an order that reflects some defined sequence for the zip code '501'.

I've tried a few approaches involving ordering the area codes and counties, attempting to link them based on their association with the zip code. However, I'm struggling to get the sequence right. The results I'm getting don't seem to correctly pair the area codes with their corresponding county information in the intended order.

How can I construct a query in PostgreSQL to list the area codes and their associated county details (county name, state) in a sequential order for the specific zip code '501'?
issue_sql:
SELECT zip_code FROM (
    SELECT 
        ac.zip_code, 
        ac.area_code, 
        co.county,
        CASE 
            WHEN ac.area_code < 700 AND lead(co.county) OVER (PARTITION BY ac.zip_code ORDER BY ac.area_code) LIKE 'S%' THEN CONCAT(ac.area_code, '_', lead(co.county) OVER (PARTITION BY ac.zip_code ORDER BY ac.area_code))
            WHEN ac.area_code >= 700 THEN CAST(ac.area_code AS TEXT)
            ELSE co.county || '_' || CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ac.zip_code ORDER BY ac.area_code) AS TEXT) -- Mimic flawed ROW_NUMBER usage
        END AS derived_value
    FROM area_code AS ac
    JOIN country AS co ON ac.zip_code = co.zip_code -- Join might produce cross product if multiple counties/area codes exist for one zip
    WHERE ac.zip_code = 501
) AS tmp
WHERE derived_value IS NOT NULL;
sol_sql:
WITH AreaCodeSequence AS (
    SELECT 
        ac.zip_code, 
        ac.area_code, 
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ac.zip_code ORDER BY ac.area_code) AS seq_num
    FROM area_code AS ac
    WHERE ac.zip_code = 501
),
CountySequence AS (
    SELECT 
        co.zip_code, 
        co.county, 
        co.state, 
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY co.zip_code ORDER BY co.county) AS seq_num
    FROM country AS co
    WHERE co.zip_code = 501
)
SELECT 
    acs.zip_code, 
    acs.area_code, 
    cs.county, 
    cs.state
FROM AreaCodeSequence AS acs
LEFT JOIN CountySequence AS cs 
  ON acs.zip_code = cs.zip_code AND acs.seq_num = cs.seq_num
ORDER BY acs.seq_num;

WITH AuthorTitleData AS (
    SELECT A.au_id AS AUTHORID, A.au_fname, A.au_lname, T.title_id, T.royalty, T.price, T.ytd_sales,

    FROM authors AS A

    LEFT JOIN titles AS T ON TA.title_id = T.title_id

My goal is to get a summary showing each month (formatted like 'YYYY-MM') and the total number of distinct days within that month that had at least one status update recorded. It doesn't matter how many updates happened on a single day, only that *at least one* update occurred on that day. I've been trying different ways to group the information by month and count the relevant days, but I'm finding it tricky to get the logic right. My attempts seem to either count every single update instead of just the unique days, or the monthly totals aren't accurate. I also need the final list to be sorted chronologically by month (e.g., '2020-08', '2021-07'), but the results I'm getting seem to be sorted alphabetically instead. How can I structure a query to correctly count the number of distinct days with status updates for each month, display the month as 'YYYY-MM', and ensure the output is ordered chronologically?
issue_sql:
WITH MonthlyStatusUpdates AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date) AS update_year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date) AS update_month,
        convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date AS update_date,
        history_id,
        order_id,
        status_id
    FROM order_history
), DailyStatusUpdatesWithRank AS (
    SELECT
        update_year,
        update_month,
        TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', update_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month_format,
        update_date,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY update_year, update_month ORDER BY update_date NULLS FIRST) AS date_rank,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY update_date) AS updates_per_day
    FROM MonthlyStatusUpdates
), DistinctDaysPerMonth AS (
    SELECT
        month_format AS month,
        MAX(date_rank) AS distinct_days
    FROM DailyStatusUpdatesWithRank
    GROUP BY month_format
)
SELECT
    d.month,
    d.distinct_days,
    (SELECT convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date FROM order_history WHERE TO_CHAR(convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date, 'YYYY-MM') = d.month LIMIT 1) AS first_update_date
FROM DistinctDaysPerMonth AS d
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        TO_CHAR(convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS total_updates
    FROM order_history
    GROUP BY TO_CHAR(convert_from(status_date, 'UTF8')::date, 'YYYY-MM')
) AS r ON d.month = r.month
ORDER BY d.month NULLS FIRST

        (ol.line_id % 3) + 1 AS pseudo_position,

        order_line AS ol

WITH ZipAverages AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(CAST(avg_income_per_household AS DECIMAL(15, 2))) AS AvgIncome,
        AVG(CAST(land_area AS DECIMAL(15, 2))) AS AvgLandArea
    FROM zip_data

WITH OrderHistoryCTE AS (
    SELECT
        O.order_id,
        O.customer_id,
        O.order_date,
        O.shipping_method_id,
        O.dest_address_id,
        LEAD(O.shipping_method_id) OVER (PARTITION BY O.customer_id ORDER BY O.order_date::text NULLS FIRST) AS next_shipping_method_id,
        LEAD(O.dest_address_id) OVER (PARTITION BY O.customer_id ORDER BY O.order_date::text NULLS FIRST) AS next_dest_address_id,
        LAG(O.shipping_method_id) OVER (PARTITION BY O.customer_id ORDER BY O.order_date::text NULLS FIRST) AS prev_shipping_method_id,
        LAG(O.dest_address_id) OVER (PARTITION BY O.customer_id ORDER BY O.order_date::text NULLS FIRST) AS prev_dest_address_id,
        COUNT(O.order_id) OVER (PARTITION BY O.customer_id) AS customer_order_count
    FROM cust_order AS O
)
SELECT

    customer_id,
    order_date,
    shipping_method_id,
    dest_address_id,
    next_shipping_method_id,
    next_dest_address_id,
    prev_shipping_method_id,
    prev_dest_address_id,
    customer_order_count
FROM OrderHistoryCTE
WHERE prev_shipping_method_id > shipping_method_id AND customer_order_count > 1
ORDER BY customer_id NULLS FIRST, order_date::text NULLS FIRST

query: I'm working with data about films available in different stores (e.g., store 1, store 2). Each film might have multiple inventory items in each store, each with its own unique inventory identifier. My goal is to produce a result that lists each film's title, the store ID, and the difference between the highest inventory identifier and the lowest inventory identifier for that specific film within that specific store. So, for a given film in store 1, I want to subtract the lowest inventory ID from the highest inventory ID. How can I structure a query to show the film title, the store ID, and calculate the difference between the highest inventory identifier and the lowest inventory identifier for films within stores 1 and 2?
issue_sql:
WITH FilmInventory AS (
    SELECT
        f.title AS film_title,
        i.store_id,
        i.inventory_id,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY f.film_id, i.store_id ORDER BY i.inventory_id ASC) AS rank_asc,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY f.film_id, i.store_id ORDER BY i.inventory_id DESC) AS rank_desc
    FROM
        film AS f
    LEFT JOIN
        inventory AS i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
    WHERE
        i.store_id IN (1, 2)
),
InventoryStats AS (
    SELECT
        film_title,
        store_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rank_desc = 1 THEN inventory_id END) AS max_inv_id, -- Analogous to 'Legal' ID
        MAX(CASE WHEN rank_asc = 1 THEN inventory_id END) AS min_inv_id  -- Analogous to 'Banned' ID
    FROM filmInventory
    GROUP BY film_title, store_id
)
SELECT
    fi.film_title,
    fi.store_id,
    ist.max_inv_id,
    ist.min_inv_id,
    CASE
        WHEN fi.rank_desc = 1 THEN ist.max_inv_id - ist.min_inv_id
        ELSE NULL
    END AS id_diff
FROM
    filmInventory AS fi
JOIN
    InventoryStats AS ist ON fi.film_title = ist.film_title AND fi.store_id = ist.store_id
WHERE fi.rank_asc = 1 OR fi.rank_desc = 1
ORDER BY
    fi.film_title ASC NULLS FIRST,
    fi.store_id ASC NULLS FIRST

SELECT
    f.title AS film_title,
    i.store_id,
    MAX(i.inventory_id) OVER (PARTITION BY f.title, i.store_id) AS max_inventory_id,
    MIN(i.inventory_id) OVER (PARTITION BY f.title, i.store_id) AS min_inventory_id,
    CASE
        WHEN i.inventory_id = MAX(i.inventory_id) OVER (PARTITION BY f.title, i.store_id)
        THEN (MAX(i.inventory_id) OVER (PARTITION BY f.title, i.store_id) - MIN(i.inventory_id) OVER (PARTITION BY f.title, i.store_id))
        ELSE NULL
    END AS id_diff
FROM
    film AS f
INNER JOIN
    inventory AS i ON f.film_id = i.film_id
WHERE
    i.store_id IN (1, 2)
ORDER BY
    f.title ASC NULLS FIRST,
    i.store_id ASC NULLS FIRST

WITH CompetitorMedals AS (
    SELECT p.full_name AS competitor_name, e.event_name, m.medal_name, m.id,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.id, e.id ORDER BY CASE WHEN m.medal_name = 'Gold' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END NULLS FIRST) AS medal_priority
    FROM person AS p
    JOIN games_competitor AS gc ON p.id = gc.person_id
    JOIN competitor_event AS ce ON gc.id = ce.competitor_id
    JOIN event AS e ON ce.event_id = e.id
    JOIN medal AS m ON ce.medal_id = m.id
    WHERE e.event_name IN ('Basketball Men''s Basketball', 'Judo Men''s Extra-Lightweight', 'Football Men''s Football')
),
MedalStats AS (
    SELECT competitor_name, event_name,
    MAX(CASE WHEN medal_name = 'Gold' THEN id END) AS gold_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN medal_name = 'Bronze' THEN id END) AS bronze_id
    FROM CompetitorMedals
    GROUP BY competitor_name, event_name
)
SELECT cm.competitor_name, cm.event_name, ms.gold_id, ms.bronze_id,
CASE WHEN cm.medal_name = 'Gold' AND cm.medal_priority = 1 THEN ms.gold_id - ms.bronze_id END AS id_diff
FROM CompetitorMedals AS cm
JOIN MedalStats AS ms ON cm.competitor_name = ms.competitor_name AND cm.event_name = ms.event_name
WHERE cm.medal_name IN ('Gold', 'Bronze')
ORDER BY cm.competitor_name ASC NULLS FIRST, cm.event_name ASC NULLS FIRST

My goal is to generate a list where, for every customer, each payment date is shown next to the date of their *previous* payment. I also want to include sequence numbers for these paired dates.

I've experimented with using window functions to partition the data by customer and order it by date, allowing me to look up the prior date. This seems to give me the right pairs (previous date, current date, sequence numbers) when I specifically filter the results for one customer, for example, customer ID 1.

However, I'm stuck on how to apply this logic efficiently across *all* customers. I need the output to include these date pairs for everyone in the table, not just the single customer I tested with. I'm not sure if I should be filtering differently or if my overall approach needs adjustment to scale to the entire dataset.

How can I get this list of consecutive payment dates (previous and current) along with their sequence numbers for all customers, instead of just for a single customer like 1?

query: I'm trying to figure out which zip codes possess all the area codes associated with certain 'state IDs' in my dataset. I have information linking zip codes to their individual area codes and separate information linking state IDs to the area codes they require. My goal is to get a list of state ID and zip code pairs where the zip code has every single area code listed for that state ID (they might have additional area codes too, which is fine). I've attempted to join the zip code area code data with the state ID area code requirements and then count the number of matching area codes for each state ID-zip code combination. I then tried to compare this count against the total number of area codes required for the state ID. However, the results I'm getting seem wrong. It seems like my current approach is only finding zip codes who have *more* matching area codes than the total required for the state ID, which doesn't seem logically possible and excludes the zip codes I actually want to find – those who have *at least* all the required area codes. For instance, if a state ID needs area codes 631 and 718, and a zip code has area codes 631, 718, and 512, that zip code should be considered a match for that state ID, but my current query isn't identifying such cases. How can I structure my query correctly to compare the count of matched area codes with the total required area codes for each state ID, so that I only get the pairs where the zip code possesses *at least* all the area codes listed for that specific state ID?
issue_sql: WITH pages AS (SELECT 1 AS state_id, 631 AS area_code UNION ALL SELECT 1, 718 UNION ALL SELECT 2, 631 UNION ALL SELECT 3, 631 UNION ALL SELECT 3, 718 UNION ALL SELECT 3, 212 UNION ALL SELECT 4, 512 UNION ALL SELECT 5, 305 UNION ALL SELECT 5, 631 UNION ALL SELECT 6, 631 UNION ALL SELECT 6, 907), items AS (SELECT 501 AS zip_code, 631 AS area_code UNION ALL SELECT 501, 718 UNION ALL SELECT 501, 512 UNION ALL SELECT 601, 631 UNION ALL SELECT 601, 305) SELECT p.state_id, i.zip_code FROM (SELECT p.state_id, p.area_code, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY p.state_id) AS total_codes FROM pages AS p) AS p INNER JOIN items AS i ON p.area_code = i.area_code GROUP BY p.state_id, i.zip_code, p.total_codes HAVING COUNT(i.area_code) > p.total_codes

Once I've identified these orders (the ones with multiple distinct books), I then need to find out, for each one, which of its book IDs is numerically smallest. So, if an order had book IDs 25, 5, and 10, I'd want to identify it as having multiple distinct books, and then retrieve just the book ID 5 for it. How can I construct a query to filter for orders that have at least two different book IDs, and then for each of these orders, return only the single book ID that is numerically smallest?
issue_sql:
WITH BookIdRanking AS (
    SELECT line_id, order_id, book_id, book_id AS book_id_rank -- Simple rank based on ID
    FROM order_line
), OrderWithMultipleBooks AS (
    SELECT order_id
    FROM order_line
    GROUP BY order_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT book_id) > 1 -- Simplified distinct count
)
SELECT b.order_id, b.book_id
FROM (
    SELECT bir.order_id, bir.book_id,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bir.order_id ORDER BY bir.book_id_rank NULLS FIRST, LENGTH(CAST(bir.book_id AS TEXT)) NULLS FIRST, bir.book_id NULLS FIRST) AS rn -- Mimic complex order
    FROM BookIdRanking AS bir
    INNER JOIN OrderWithMultipleBooks AS m ON bir.order_id = m.order_id
    -- WHERE NOT bir.book_id_rank IS NULL -- Original query had a condition here, potentially redundant if book_id is NOT NULL
) AS b
WHERE b.rn = 1
ORDER BY b.order_id NULLS FIRST -- Simplified final order based on target schema
sol_sql: SELECT order_id, book_id FROM (SELECT ol.order_id, ol.book_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ol.order_id ORDER BY ol.book_id NULLS FIRST) AS rn FROM order_line AS ol WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM order_line AS ol0 WHERE ol0.order_id = ol.order_id GROUP BY ol0.order_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ol0.book_id) > 1)) AS w WHERE rn = 1

I'm working with book publishing data in PostgreSQL and trying to find the specific book title published by a publisher in 'Berkeley' city that has the highest year-to-date sales. I'm only interested in titles identified as type 'business'.

My goal is to get a single result showing the name of this top title, along with its year-to-date sales, price, and royalty.

I've tried combining the title information with the publisher data and filtering for 'Berkeley' city and type 'business' titles. However, I'm having trouble isolating *only* the title with the absolute highest year-to-date sales across all type 'business' titles from that city. My attempts either return multiple titles, no titles, or don't seem to correctly identify the single top one based on the sales figure. I feel like I'm missing the right way to compare the sales and pull out just the maximum.

How can I structure my query to correctly find the single type 'business' title from a 'Berkeley' publisher with the highest year-to-date sales and return its title name, YTD sales, price, and royalty?
issue_sql:
WITH TitleSales AS (
    SELECT
        t.title,
        t.ytd_sales,
        t.price,
        t.royalty,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t.type ORDER BY t.ytd_sales DESC) AS SalesRank
    FROM
        titles AS t
    INNER JOIN
        publishers AS p ON t.pub_id = p.pub_id
    WHERE
        p.city = 'Berkeley'
        AND t.type = 'business'
),
MaxYTDSales AS (
    SELECT MAX(t.ytd_sales) AS MaxSales
    FROM titles AS t
    INNER JOIN publishers AS p ON t.pub_id = p.pub_id
    WHERE p.city = 'Berkeley' AND t.type = 'business'
)
SELECT
    ts.title,
    ts.ytd_sales,
    ts.price,
    ts.royalty
FROM
    TitleSales ts
CROSS JOIN
    MaxYTDSales mys
WHERE
    ts.ytd_sales = mys.MaxSales
    AND ts.SalesRank > 1
ORDER BY
    ts.ytd_sales DESC;
sol_sql:
SELECT t.title, t.ytd_sales, t.price, t.royalty
FROM titles AS t
INNER JOIN publishers AS p ON t.pub_id = p.pub_id
WHERE p.city = 'Berkeley' AND t.type = 'business'
ORDER BY t.ytd_sales DESC
LIMIT 1;

I'm working with movie rental data in PostgreSQL and trying to find the specific film with a 'PG' rating in the 'Action' category that has the highest rental rate. My goal is to get a single result showing the title of this top film, along with its rental rate, length, and replacement cost.

I've tried combining the film information with category data and filtering for 'PG' rating and the 'Action' category. However, I'm having trouble isolating *only* the film with the absolute highest rental rate across all 'Action' films with a 'PG' rating. My attempts either return multiple films, no films, or don't seem to correctly identify the single top one based on the rental rate. I feel like I'm missing the right way to compare the rates and pull out just the maximum.

How can I structure my query to correctly find the single 'PG' rated film in the 'Action' category with the highest rental rate and return its title, rental rate, length, and replacement cost?
issue_sql:
WITH FilmRates AS (
    SELECT
        f.title,
        f.rental_rate,
        f.length,
        f.replacement_cost,
        cat.name AS category_name,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cat.name ORDER BY f.rental_rate DESC) AS RentalRank
    FROM
        film AS f
    INNER JOIN
        film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    INNER JOIN
        category AS cat ON fc.category_id = cat.category_id
    WHERE
        f.rating = 'PG'
        AND cat.name = 'Action'
),
MaxRentalRate AS (
    SELECT MAX(f.rental_rate) AS MaxRate
    FROM film AS f
    INNER JOIN film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    INNER JOIN category AS cat ON fc.category_id = cat.category_id
    WHERE cat.name = 'Action'
)
SELECT
    fr.title,
    fr.rental_rate,
    fr.length,
    fr.replacement_cost
FROM
    FilmRates fr
CROSS JOIN
    MaxRentalRate mrr
WHERE
    fr.rental_rate = mrr.MaxRate
    AND fr.RentalRank > 1
ORDER BY
    fr.rental_rate DESC;

SELECT f.title, f.rental_rate, f.length, f.replacement_cost
FROM film AS f
INNER JOIN film_category AS fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
INNER JOIN category AS cat ON fc.category_id = cat.category_id
WHERE f.rating = 'PG' AND cat.name = 'Action'
ORDER BY f.rental_rate DESC
LIMIT 1;

I need to create an XML report from my PostgreSQL database, and I want the final result as a single text string. The report needs a specific structure: a root element called 'Results', which should contain two main parts. The first part, under an element named 'Columns', needs to list details about the columns from one of my tables – specifically, the column name and its data type from the `zip_data` table. The second part, under an element named 'Rows', should list actual data records from another table (`country`), including fields like a `zip_code` identifier and a `county` name for each record.

I've been experimenting with PostgreSQL's XML capabilities to build this. My attempts involved fetching the column metadata and the data rows, and then trying to assemble them into the required nested XML format. However, getting the 'Columns' and 'Rows' elements correctly nested inside the 'Results' element, and then getting the whole thing as text, has been challenging. The structure often doesn't come out quite right.

Could someone guide me on how to generate this specific XML structure (Results > Columns > Column details, and Results > Rows > Row data) and output the entire structure as a single text string in PostgreSQL?

DECLARE
    xml_result xml;
BEGIN
    -- First attempt to build the XML structure with nested XML queries
    WITH SchemaInfo AS (
        SELECT
            COLUMN_NAME,
            DATA_TYPE,
            ORDINAL_POSITION
        FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
        WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'zip_data' AND TABLE_SCHEMA = current_schema()
    ),
    AddressData AS (
        SELECT
            zip_code,
            county
        FROM country
    )

    SELECT xmlelement(
        name "Results",
        (SELECT xmlagg(
            xmlelement(
                name "Columns",
                (SELECT xmlagg(
                    xmlelement(
                        name "Column",
                        xmlattributes(COLUMN_NAME as "Name"),
                        xmlelement(name "DataType", DATA_TYPE)
                    )
                )
                FROM SchemaInfo
                ORDER BY ORDINAL_POSITION)
            )
        )),
        (SELECT xmlagg(
            xmlelement(
                name "Rows",
                (SELECT xmlagg(
                    xmlelement(
                        name "Row",
                        xmlelement(name "zip_code", CASE WHEN zip_code IS NULL THEN 'xsi:nil="true"' ELSE zip_code::text END),
                        xmlelement(name "county", CASE WHEN county IS NULL THEN 'xsi:nil="true"' ELSE county END)
                    )
                )
                FROM AddressData)
            )
        ))
    ) INTO xml_result;

    -- Attempt to extract specific nodes using XPath that doesn't match the structure
    SELECT xpath('/Results/Rows/Row', xml_result)::text AS RowsXml,
           xpath('/Results/Columns/Column', xml_result)::text AS ColumnsXml,
           (xpath('/Results', xml_result))[1]::text AS EntireXmlAsText;
END $$;
